source.title: A Granular Study of Safety Pretraining under Model Abliteration
source.authors: Shashank Agnihotri; Jonas Jakubassa; Priyam Dey; Sachin Goyal; B. Schiele; Venkatesh Babu Radhakrishnan; Margret Keuper

record.tranche_reason: The study uses inference-time abliteration as an attack to evaluate the robustness of safety-pretraining checkpoints. Its results concern refusal behavior under this edit, but it does not test the claim versions about fine-tuning on harmful or benign examples, token-position KL, compliant prefills/suffixes/decoding, localized weights, or safety depth beyond initial tokens.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-refusal outcomes before and after abliteration, which is an activation-space projection rather than the interventions or measurements named by the claim versions. These outcomes are recorded as related findings under versions ["none"]. Its cited claims about benign fine-tuning, adversarial prompting, and refusal directions are background, not this study's results. Figures contain count bars, but the provided text does not give reliably assignable per-model ChatGPT5 counts; the appendix table is flattened and does not support confident mapping of all values.
record.test_reason: The study's only intervention is inference-time abliteration: projecting out one PCA 'refusal direction' from residual activations, with no weight change. That is not fine-tuning (V1/V2), per-token KL (V3), a prefill, suffix or decoding change (V4), weight or rank localization (V5), a cause of token-position shallowness (V6), or a deepening method (V7). The paper does not use the shallow-alignment finding as a tool. Qi et al. (an original source) is cited only as background on benign fine-tuning. The findings are a related construct (activation-direction removal) and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right as a paraphrase: the authors say rephrase-only and refusal-only stages are easy to neutralize and that combined ingredients are more robust, and they recommend including activation edits in safety evaluation. However, their own ChatGPT5 counts show Score0+Rephrase+Refusals unchanged (48 to 48) and Raw Data nearly unchanged (46 to 45). The 'refusal-only fragile' conclusion is therefore not clearly supported by the reconstructed numbers.
record.recipe_differences: The intervention is inference-time activation projection derived from a harmful/harmless anchor set, not fine-tuning, prefilled tokens, decoding changes, or a weight edit. It evaluates checkpoint robustness to abliteration.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by checkpoint/model: the authors report the largest baseline drop for Llama-3.3, no loss for Qwen3, and greater robustness for combined Safety Pretraining ingredients. Evaluation outcomes are also judge-sensitive; ChatGPT5 is selected as the primary judge after comparison with other judges.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing one PCA refusal direction at inference cuts harmful refusals strongly for SmolLM2-Instruct (35 to 15) and Score0+Rephrase (49 to 34). Most other checkpoints and Qwen3 change little or not at all (ChatGPT5 judge, n=50).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in some models is mediated by a single removable activation direction, and robustness to its removal depends on model family and pretraining data recipe.

record.problems: The paper states that human validation covers only 200 of 2,000 prompt-response pairs and that no error bars or significance tests are reported. The main outcome counts are presented in figures; the provided flattened figure/table text does not permit reliable assignment of all per-model counts. The authors also note that results concern open weights and inference-time activation edits, and that finer-grained safety-pretraining factors were not tested.
record.rows_left_out: No separately mapped counts for judges other than ChatGPT5 or for harmless prompts are included: these do not test a listed claim version, and the supplied flattened figure text does not support reliable per-model assignment. Judge-comparison correlations and self-judgment findings concern evaluation reliability rather than the claim versions.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or token-position analysis.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks. Abliteration is an activation edit.
No weight or rank localization. A single activation direction is removed without changing weights.
No test of what causes token-depth shallowness. Safety-pretraining ingredients are compared only under abliteration.
No method spreading safety beyond the first tokens is trained or evaluated.

missing.what: Per-model ChatGPT5 harmful-refusal counts before and after abliteration for the 9 models other than Llama (e.g. SmolLM2 35 to 15, Score0+Rephrase 49 to 34, Qwen3 45 to 46). These should fill the rows' baseline and value fields.

record.verdict_notes: Abliteration relates to refusal-direction work (Arditi et al.), not to token-depth shallow alignment. No error bars; n=50 harmful prompts per model. Values were reconstructed from flattened figure text, so the column mapping should be verified against the PDF.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully chosen benign data.
No per-token KL measurement or comparison of aligned and base models.
No compliant opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test; abliteration is a different intervention.
No weight/rank localization test; the edit projects activations at inference time without changing model weights.
No test of whether training data or objective causes safety to be shallow in response-token positions.
The paper compares safety-pretraining ingredients under abliteration, but does not train or measure a method designed to spread safety beyond the first response tokens.

rows.subject: SmolLM2
rows.operation_detail: Inference-time PCA projection removing a refusal-sensitive activation direction; parameters not updated.
rows.note: Text says harmful-refusal drops sharply after abliteration for base SmolLM2; per-model count could not be reliably read from the supplied figure/table text.
rows.check: Values can be read from the Fig. 4 ChatGPT5 row: harmful refusals 35/50 before, 15/50 after abliteration. Fill in baseline and value.

rows.subject: Raw Data
rows.operation_detail: Inference-time PCA projection removing a refusal-sensitive activation direction; parameters not updated.
rows.note: Text groups Raw Data among stages that lose harmful refusal under the attack; exact paired count not reliably assignable from the flattened table.
rows.check: Fig. 4 ChatGPT5 row gives Raw Data 46 before, 45 after: a negligible change. This contradicts the text's claim that it loses refusal. Reconstructed from flattened figure text; verify.

rows.subject: Score 0
rows.operation_detail: Inference-time PCA projection removing a refusal-sensitive activation direction; parameters not updated.
rows.note: Text states Score 0 also loses harmful refusal under the attack; exact paired count not reliably assignable from the flattened table.
rows.check: Fig. 4 ChatGPT5 row gives Score 0 46 before, 41 after: a small drop, not a sharp loss. Fill in values.

rows.subject: Score 0 + Rephrase
rows.operation_detail: Inference-time PCA projection removing a refusal-sensitive activation direction; parameters not updated.
rows.note: Authors say this checkpoint refuses many harmful prompts before abliteration and many become not refused after it; the exact paired counts are not reliably assignable.
rows.check: Fig. 4 ChatGPT5 row gives 49 before, 34 after. Fill in values.

rows.subject: Score 0 + Rephrase data + Metatags
rows.operation_detail: Inference-time PCA projection removing a refusal-sensitive activation direction; parameters not updated.
rows.note: Authors describe a small change after abliteration and high harmful-refusal retention, but not complete immunity.
rows.check: Fig. 4 ChatGPT5 row gives 46 before, 46 after: no change.

rows.subject: Score 0 + Rephrase data + Refusals
rows.operation_detail: Inference-time PCA projection removing a refusal-sensitive activation direction; parameters not updated.
rows.note: Authors state that adding refusals to rephrase data reduces the attack's effect; exact paired counts are not reliably assignable.
rows.check: Fig. 4 ChatGPT5 row gives 48 before, 48 after. This conflicts with the conclusion that refusal-only stages are 'easy to neutralize'. Reconstructed from flattened text; verify.

rows.subject: Safety Oracle
rows.operation_detail: Inference-time PCA projection removing a refusal-sensitive activation direction; parameters not updated.
rows.note: The full recipe combining safe-only filtering, rephrasing, refusals, and metatags is described as strongest, with harmful prompts largely refused before and after and the smallest pre/post gap among Safety Pretraining variants.
rows.check: Fig. 4 ChatGPT5 row gives Safety Oracle 49 before, 47 after: near-absent change.

rows.subject: GLM-4
rows.operation_detail: Inference-time PCA projection removing a refusal-sensitive activation direction; parameters not updated.
rows.note: Authors state that GLM-4 loses harmful refusal after abliteration; exact paired counts are not reliably assignable.
rows.check: Fig. 4 ChatGPT5 row gives GLM-4 47 before, 45 after: a small drop, despite the text saying it 'loses harmful-refusal'.

rows.subject: Llama-3.3
rows.operation_detail: Inference-time PCA projection removing a refusal-sensitive activation direction; parameters not updated.
rows.note: Authors state that Llama-3.3 loses harmful refusal after abliteration and has the largest drop among the open-weight baselines.
rows.check: Llama-3.3 is absent from the Fig. 4 and Fig. 6 grids. Its Fig. 2 bars are not readable from the text, so the 'largest drop' claim is text-only.

rows.subject: Qwen3
rows.operation_detail: Inference-time PCA projection removing a refusal-sensitive activation direction; parameters not updated.
